capabilities.target: ERP vendor master including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The design relies on a one line model summary for approval rather than exposing raw payment destination and bank change details to the reviewer.

elements.name: Supplier invoice upload into agent context
Scheduled payment instruction leaving the agent to ERP/banking workflow
ERP vendor master and bank details

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only a model generated one line summary, not raw action details. A more capable model can omit or frame destination and bank change details more persuasively, and approval fatigue is already high at roughly 150 cards per day.

controls.name: Raw action approval showing destination account and change history
Scoped ERP credentials limited to approved vendors and payment actions

findings.title: Summary gated irreversible payment and bank change from untrusted invoice (TC9)

attack_path.note: Untrusted supplier supplied content can request or imply new bank details and payment instructions.
The agent can update any vendor bank details with broad ERP credentials.
The agent can schedule payment using the updated destination after clerk approval of only a one line summary.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version changes without separate review, approval flow is loosened or removed, or approval volume/task horizon rises beyond the current roughly 150 cards per day.

evidence.observation: The prompt directs the agent to process supplier invoices, update vendor bank details when the invoice shows new details, and schedule payment.
The clerk sees only a one line summary: Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521).
The card omits bank account numbers and change history, so the approver cannot verify the raw destination or whether the bank details changed.
The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, which is high approval volume and increases approval fatigue.
The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment, so the agent operates with broad authority.
The model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so the summary based approval control is exposed to model_upgrade.

recommendations.action: Replace summary only approval with raw action approval that shows vendor identity, current and proposed bank account details, payment destination, and change history before any bank update or payment scheduling.
Scope ERP credentials so the agent cannot update arbitrary vendors or schedule unrestricted payments without an independent workflow binding the approved vendor and destination.

findings.title: Broad ERP authority creates confused deputy exposure for vendor bank changes and payment scheduling (TC4)

attack_path.note: Untrusted supplier content can initiate actions.
Broad ERP credential permits updates to any vendor.
Broad ERP credential permits scheduling any payment.

forecast.watch_signal: Any reduction or bypass of clerk approval, or platform model change without review, leaves broad ERP authority directly reachable from untrusted invoice content.

evidence.observation: The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment.
Supplier invoice content drives vendor matching, bank update decisions, and payment scheduling.
The sole blocking control is a summary based clerk approval rather than a destination bound workflow.

recommendations.action: Replace broad ERP credentials with least privilege scopes and bind approval to the exact vendor, bank destination, and payment amount that may be executed.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no inbound authentication surface or impersonable agent identity for the subject agent itself.
The artifacts do not show self modification or mutable tool definitions for this agent, only invoice processing and approval flow.
The assessed present design exposes no separate data exfiltration channel beyond payment execution, which is covered as a payment misuse path instead.
No loop, recursive delegation, spend runaway, or availability impacting behavior is described in the available artifacts.
The artifacts do not describe portal authentication or supplier identity verification, so impersonation resistance cannot be evaluated.
The artifacts do not say whether supplier submissions are attributable to authenticated identities with retained records.
This inbound boundary flow carries supplier provided invoice data into the agent and is not described as exposing internal data outward.
No evidence shows this inbound flow can exhaust resources or trigger open ended processing in the declared design.
The boundary crossing is a payment instruction rather than disclosure of internal records to an external consumer in the provided design.
The artifacts do not show high volume autonomous retries or queue flooding on this outbound payment scheduling flow.
The design shows reads of confidential vendor master data, but tenant separation and disclosure controls for the ERP store are not described.
No destructive or high volume write pattern against the vendor master is described beyond individual bank detail updates.
The artifacts do not state whether approval records are immutable or tamper evident once a clerk acts on the card.
The approval record shown contains little detail and the available artifacts do not indicate secret leakage from this store.
The design does not describe quota exhaustion, storage contention, or record unavailability concerns for the approval record store.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by an untrusted supplier invoice reaching broad bank update and payment scheduling capabilities. The only declared preventive control is a high volume human approval gate that shows a model summary rather than raw action details, so rubric step 2 reduces inherent critical by one tier to high and cannot lower the result below moderate. Forecast rises to critical if model upgrades, autonomy increases, or the gate is weakened or removed, because the named approval control is partially dependent and already stressed by approval fatigue. Manual validation was applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt, approval card, and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, ERP workflow configuration, or audit logging specification was provided, so capability wiring and record integrity were assessed from the described design only.

No runtime evidence was available to verify whether the approval card is cryptographically bound to the actual payment and bank change record, so controls were treated as declared rather than verified.
